Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-02 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no identification was revealed to me in context beforehand)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context proposed an identification of this text. I have not tried to identify work or author. (I read packet-01 immediately before this one, as instructed; the two leaves look alike in script and layout, but I have not carried any reading over from one to the other.)

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)

Two faces of one parchment leaf mounted on a modern paper guard.
- Face A: overview image-001; tiles image-002 .. image-007. Modern foliation "7" top right; round red library stamp in the lower left margin (legend begins "BIBLIOTHEQ..."; rest unread).
- Face B: overview image-008; tiles image-009 .. image-014.

Observations:
- Upright, two columns per face, about 31 lines per column. No running title.
- Rounded minuscule, brown ink, frequent run-together words; "&" inside words (uid&, defl&, ph&a); punctuation "·;" ; "&cr" for et cetera. Sentence initials slightly enlarged; on Face B several are filled with orange-red (Q, D, A, S, E, P, M); on Face A they are uncoloured.
- One rubric, in orange-red minuscule, at the foot of the left column of Face B (two short lines, damaged; see section 5). No large decorated initial survives.
- Interlinear corrections by a contemporary hand: single letters or syllables added above the line (e.g. "n" over "comutantur", "ci" over "auaricia", "ci" over a word in Face A right col., small strokes over "relabi").
- A faint marginal note in the outer margin of Face A beside right-column line 16 (two words, unread, begins "Ip.."?).
- Damage: Face A right column is rubbed along its right edge and its first four lines are nearly gone; the foot of that column is lost to mould and tearing. Face B has lost the lower left corner (the left column ends in a torn edge just under the rubric), is rubbed and creased in the left column, and has a large brown stain and a vertical run across the right column. Faint offset or erased pen-flourishes show through in the right column of Face B.

Tentative interpretation (not observation): continuous prose exposition in which short quoted lemmata (after "·;" with an enlarged capital, often ended "&cr") alternate with comment; "Unde & subditur" recurs as the transition into the next lemma. The rubric on Face B appears to mark the start of a new section, whose text begins at the top of the right column. Which face is recto is not determinable from the images; the sense suggests Face A precedes Face B.

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD

Selected: all four columns line by line. Face A left column is read in full. Face A right column: lines 5-25 read with gaps at the line-ends. Face B: both columns read with uncertain words marked.
Unread: Face A right column lines 1-4 (only scattered words) and 26-30; the marginal note; the stamp; Face B left column lines 25-27; some stained words in Face B right column.
A UV or raking-light image of the top right of Face A and the foot of Face B would help.

Conventions: (..) = my expansion; ? after a word = uncertain; [illegible] = unreadable; [lost] = parchment missing. Line numbers count text lines from the top of the named tile (a line cut by the tile edge is still counted). Overlaps between tiles are noted and given once.

7. LIMITATIONS

- Face A right column lines 1-4 and 26-30 and Face B left column lines 25-27 are largely unrecovered; the damage there is real (abrasion, mould, loss), but a better image might yield more.
- The rubric reading is weak: I am confident only that it is two short lines of orange-red script containing a numeral and "p...cos" in the first line and a word ending in "-ca(m)"/"-cu(m)" in the second.
- Readings under the brown stain in Face B right column (lines 15-17 and 24-28 of the column) are partly conjectural letter-matching and are marked "?".
- Per-tile line numbers may be off by one where the tile edge cuts a line.
- Column order (left then right) assumed; order of the two faces not established from the images.
- Orthography is kept as seen (e.g. "occuli", "gingere", "sterelis", "parturris", "ingresus", "henim", "habrahe", "nupcias", "adolatores"); some of these may be my misreadings of o/e, c/t, u/a.
